title: Rolling 18M budget + headcount + pricing sensitivity analysis
content:
Purpose:
This working doc holds a rolling 18-month view combining (1) operating budget by major bucket, (2) a phased headcount plan by function and hire-level costs, and (3) pricing sensitivity tests (3 scenarios) focused on ARR, gross margin and CAC payback. This is an operational model intended for finance + product + GTM alignment ahead of Q2 planning.

Key assumptions (summary):
- Time horizon: rolling 18 months starting 2026-04 (Q2 2026) through 2027-09.
- Currency: USD.
- Revenue drivers: hosted API usage (tokens), Dedicated contracts (committed monthly revenue), and Private deployment licensing.
- Baseline pricing: current list price per 1M tokens = $7.00 (hosted), average Dedicated ARR: $120k/customer/year, private licensing median deal $300k/year.
- Elasticities are segment-specific (see pricing sensitivity section).
- Hiring: average fully-loaded cost per hire depends on level. Assumed blended fully-loaded on-target cost: IC-1: $150k, IC-2: $200k, Sr IC: $280k, Mgr: $340k, Dir+: $450k (includes benefits, hiring overhead, ramp).
- Ramp assumptions: new hire revenue impact begins at 50% productivity month 3, 80% month 6, 100% month 9 for customer-facing roles. Engineering ramp slower for shipped throughput improvements.
- CAC and Sales efficiency: baseline CAC payback = 11 months; this changes under pricing scenarios.

High-level 18M operating budget (aggregated by quarter) - summary table (USD, thousands)
CSV format: Quarter,Hosted Rev, Dedicated Rev, Private Rev, Total Rev, COGS, R&D, S&M, G&A, Total OpEx, EBITDA

Notes on budget: hosted revenue growth partially driven by price/pack changes in scenario tests; Dedicated growth driven by two expected mid-size new customers in H2-2026 (closed-probability 60% in baseline). Private sales pipeline has longer sales cycle; assume initial bookings in Q4-2026 under baseline. COGS includes infra (GPU amortization, cloud egress), inference ops, and third-party licensing; COGS assumed to scale ~25% of hosted token revenue and 15% of Dedicated/Private recurring revenue in baseline.

Headcount plan (by function and quarter) - phased hires (summary)
CSV format: Role,Function,Level,Start Quarter,Planned Hires,Notes

Hiring phasing commentary: total net new headcount planned over 18 months = 16 FTEs. Hiring cadence front-loads infra and SRE in Q2 to enable Dedicated capacity increases. Customer facing hires spread into Q2/Q3 aligned to expected closed deals. We model hiring slippage (30% risk) separately in sensitivity sheet.

Unit economics and per-hire P&L impact (annualized example)
- Blended revenue per AE (ramped): $600k ARR; baseline AE ramp to quota by month 9.
- Blended gross margin baseline: 65% across product mix.
- Incremental cost of hired engineers primarily in R&D/COGS; for each backend hire we model a 0.5% reduction in per-token COGS over 12 months when combined with optimizer hires due to better batching and caching.

Pricing sensitivity analysis (3 scenarios)
Scenario A - Baseline (current price and packaging):
- Hosted: $7/1M tokens. Growth: organic +20% q/q early then moderating.
- Dedicated: committed ARR closes at baseline probability rates.
- Private deals: slow; conservative recognition schedule.
Result: ARR path matches budget table above; unit economics stable.

Scenario B - Upside (price increase & premium packaging):
- Action: 10% list price increase for hosted, introduce Premium SLA tier (+30% price for 15% of traffic), accelerate Dedicated pricing uplift (average deal size +15%).
- Elasticity assumptions: price elasticity of hosted demand = -0.12 (low elasticity for core API traffic), premium adoption = 15% of customers in 6 months.
- Secondary effects: CAC increases 8% due to more product friction in sign-up.
Impact: +8-11% revenue uplift by Q4-2026, gross margin improves by 200-400bps due to price leverage. CAC payback extends ~1 month.

Scenario C - Promotional / Competitive pressure (price cuts & higher churn):
- Action: 15% temporary discount for 4 months to protect market share vs new lower-cost open model entrants; introduce short-term free-tier expansion for small developers.
- Elasticity assumptions: short-term demand elasticity = 0.45 (usage-sensitive segment expands), enterprise Dedicated renewals unaffected but new deal conversion slows 10%.
- Secondary effects: churn among bargain-seeking customers rises 6% post-promo; retention programs increase S&M costs by 20% for 6 months.
Impact: short-term revenue bump on hosted (+10% hosted revenue during promo), but net ARR and gross margin decays by end of 18 months unless retention investment succeeds; overall EBITDA depressed by 300–500k in first 3 quarters following the promo.

Sensitivity tables (delta to baseline by scenario) - sample slices
CSV format: Metric,ScenarioB_%change,ScenarioC_%change
Total Rev (FY rolling 12m),+10%,-6%
Gross Margin (bps),+250bps,-420bps
EBITDA (annualized),+1.2M,-1.1M
CAC Payback (months),+1.0,+0.5
Net New Hires (18m),+1 (accelerated hiring),-2 (hiring freeze optional)

Risk & mitigation notes:
- Hiring slippage risk (30%): model conservative case where hires are pushed 2 quarters; consequence is slower product improvements and delayed COGS reductions. Finance contingency: maintain 12% headroom in op-ex for 6 months.
- Pricing backlash risk: monitor NPX and developer churn weekly; if NPX drops >0.5pt, pause price changes and run segmented promo tests.
- Dedicated conversion risk: pilot a 30-day ramp program for two pilot customers to de-risk Q3 bookings.

Action items (near term):
- Finance to publish the full model (spreadsheet) with toggles for elasticity and hiring slippage (owner: Maya) by 2026-03-05. Linked Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/FIN/rolling-18m-model
- Product + Eng to estimate realistic COGS reduction per backend hire and optimization workstream (owner: Ben Kline) by 2026-02-28.
- GTM to prepare a price-communication plan and segmented experiments for premium tier (owner: Aisha Raman) by 2026-03-10.

Open questions (for leadership):
1) Tolerance for temporary margin compression to defend share in hosted? (range suggested: tolerate -250bps for up to 3 quarters).
2) Hiring priority if we must cut: preserve infra/SRE vs GTM? Recs: preserve infra + 50% of planned SRE, pause 1 AE.
3) Commitment to Dedicated sales milestones—should we accelerate incentives for early renewals to hit Q4 targets?

Appendix (small excerpt of model logic and formulas):
- Hosted revenue per quarter = sum(customers_i) * usage_i * price_per_1M_tokens / 1M.
- COGS hosted = hosted_token_cost_base * total_tokens + ops_surcharge (hosted_token_cost_base initial = $1.75/1M tokens baseline).
- Gross margin = (Total Rev - COGS) / Total Rev.
- CAC payback months = (Sales + Marketing spend attributable to ACV)/ (monthly recurring revenue from new bookings)

This file is a working artifact; expect multiple updates. For the primary model spreadsheet refer to the linked Confluence page and the finance GitHub model branch.
